title: Tactical Data Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
4.     MOS 5970, Tactical Data Systems Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Tactical Data Systems (TDS) Officers supervise and
coordinate the siting, installation, operation, training, maintenance, and
repair of aviation command and control (AC2) tactical data systems (TDS), and
the Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) within the Marine Air
Command and Control System (MACCS). The TDS Officer provides the commander
with expert technical advice regarding the employment, security,
installation, and performance of ground based air defense (GBAD) and AC2 TDS
infrastructure within service, joint, coalition, and garrison environments.
Must possess a detailed working knowledge of all voice, tactical data
communications, and GBAD systems found within the Marine Air Control Group
and within the Marine Littoral Regiments. Fleet Marine Forces billet
assignments for this officer will be in the Marine Air Control Group and the
Marine Littoral Regiment. Non-Fleet Marine Forces billet assignments for the
Tactical Data Systems Officer include Training and Maintenance Officer at the
Marine Corps Communication-Electronics School, TDS Maintenance Officer at the
Marine Corps Tactical Systems Support Activity, and Acquisition Project
Officer at Marine Corps Systems Command. The Tactical Data Systems Officer
should complete the MACCS Warrant Officer course after selection to warrant
officer. PMOS is not dependent upon the completion of this course. Upon
appointment to warrant officer, PMOS 5970 is assigned.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:   secret security clearance eligibility.

        (2) This MOS may only be assigned to Warrant Officers who were
previously qualified in enlisted MOSs 5939, 5974, or 5979.

        (3) Must meet eligibility and appointment criteria as prescribed in
MCO 1040.42B, WO and LDO accession programs.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete the MACCS Warrant Officer Course (M0968K1).

            (2) MOS is assigned after the Marine is promoted to warrant officer.

        (3) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Provide advanced technical analysis during the planning,
installation, operation, maintenance and secure integration of TDS network
architectures, tactical data link systems, radio communication systems, end-
user computers, servers, and system software/firmware.

        (2) Assist in the development of training and employment plans
designed to ensure mission essential task compliance.

        (3) Supervise diagnosis, field level repairs, and modifications to
communications and data systems.

        (4) Supervises and coordinates the activities of electronic
maintenance personnel engaged in the siting, installation, operations,
maintenance, and repair of AC2 TDS within the MACCS.


                                         1-236                         Enclosure (1)
 1134                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



        (5) Informs the Commanding Officer as to the status of equipment,
progress of work, and advises on matters pertaining to this equipment.

        (6) Supervises the keeping of maintenance records and collects data
for reports.

        (7) Supervises the reporting of failures and the requisitioning,
receipt, and allocation of tools, parts, and materials.

        (8) Instructs personnel in the mission, function, use, and procedures
for operating AC2 TDS.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

        (1) First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and
Repairers 4-1011.

            (2) Mangers, All Others 11-9199.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Aviation Communication Systems Technician, 5939.

            (2) Tactical Data Systems Technician, 5974.

            (3) Tactical Air Operations/Air defense Systems Technician, 5979.

matches: Coordinate communications between air traffic control and maintenance personnel.

Tactical Data Systems (TDS) Officers supervise and coordinate the siting, installation, operation, training, maintenance, and repair of aviation command and control (AC2) tactical data systems (TDS), and the Marine Air Defense Integrated System (MADIS) within the Marine Air Command and Control System (MACCS).
Supervise and coordinate activities of technicians and technical assistants.

d. Duties (1) Provide advanced technical analysis during the planning, installation, operation, maintenance and secure integration of TDS network architectures, tactical data link systems, radio communication systems, end- user computers, servers, and system software/firmware.
(2) Assist in the development of training and employment plans designed to ensure mission essential task compliance.
(3) Supervise diagnosis, field level repairs, and modifications to communications and data systems.
Supervise the installation or operation of electronic equipment or systems.
(4) Supervises and coordinates the activities of electronic maintenance personnel engaged in the siting, installation, operations, maintenance, and repair of AC2 TDS within the MACCS.
Communicate with bases, using telephones or two-way radios to receive instructions or technical advice, or to report equipment status.
(5) Informs the Commanding Officer as to the status of equipment, progress of work, and advises on matters pertaining to this equipment.
Maintain accurate, detailed reports and records.
(6) Supervises the keeping of maintenance records and collects data for reports.
Conduct failure analyses, document results, and recommend corrective actions.
(7) Supervises the reporting of failures and the requisitioning, receipt, and allocation of tools, parts, and materials.
Instruct personnel in radiation safety procedures and demonstrate use of protective clothing and equipment.
(8) Instructs personnel in the mission, function, use, and procedures for operating AC2 TDS.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
